$schema.description: JSON Schema URL for editor completion. Studio ignores it.

id.description: Extension id, kebab-case. Studio installs it under `<publisher>.<id>`, the publisher derived from where it came from (`local` for a folder). Ids starting `studio-` or `sprintengine-` install only from Studio’s own catalogue.

studio.description: The oldest Studio it runs on, as `>=x.y.z`: at least the newest “since” of any field it uses.

engines.description: The Studio versions it runs on.

tier.description: The most authority it needs, least first: `content` (syntaxes, keybindings, status bar items, settings: data Studio draws, no approval asked), `declarative` (commands, menus, top bar items, and the skills, MCP servers and model providers it hands agents and chats), `ui` (panels, doors, settings sections, custom editors, drawn by its own code), `worker` (`main`, running in the background). Each carries what the ones below it do; a contribution above it fails validation.

description.description: One or two sentences shown with the name.

icon.description: A square image shown beside the name.

cover.description: A wide image for its listing.

screenshots.description: Images of it at work, for its listing.

license.description: Its licence, as an SPDX expression.

permissions.description: What it asks the person to allow. `content` and `declarative` extensions hold none.

main.description: The worker’s entry: a module (`.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, or `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts` loaded as written) whose `activate(studio)` (its default export, or a named `activate`) registers what it serves. Worker tier only, and required by it.

background.description: `true` keeps the worker running while the extension is on.

id.description: Command id, unique among this extension’s commands. Without `action`, running the command calls the worker method of this name (`registerMethods`, access `operate`).

title.description: Title in the command palette and in menus.

when.description: Where the command is offered. `workspace` hides it while no workspace is open. Defaults to `global`.

action.description: A Studio command this command runs. A command with an `action` is declarative and runs no extension code; one without needs the worker tier.

where.description: The menu: a backlog item’s, a file’s in the Files tree, or one of this extension’s own notifications.

command.description: A command this extension contributes. Its title is the menu item’s label, and it runs with the item it was picked on.

id.description: Id, unique among this extension’s top bar items.

command.description: A contributed command the button runs. Give `command` or `door`, not both.

door.description: A contributed door the button opens.

icon.description: Glyph beside the title. Defaults to `extension`.

entry.description: What the panel draws, as a tab in a workspace’s pane. A module (`.js`, `.mjs`, or `.ts`, `.mts`, `.tsx`, `.jsx` loaded as written) whose `mount(root, studio)` draws into `root` and may return a cleanup function; it imports only its own files, by relative paths.

panels.description: Pane tabs, offered by the pane’s + menu.

icon.description: Glyph beside the title. Defaults to `extension`.

entry.description: What the door draws when it is open. A module (`.js`, `.mjs`, or `.ts`, `.mts`, `.tsx`, `.jsx` loaded as written) whose `mount(root, studio)` draws into `root` and may return a cleanup function; it imports only its own files, by relative paths.

doors.description: Full-window surfaces, opened from the Extensions drawer.

icon.description: Glyph beside the title. Defaults to `extension`.

entry.description: What the section draws in Settings. A module (`.js`, `.mjs`, or `.ts`, `.mts`, `.tsx`, `.jsx` loaded as written) whose `mount(root, studio)` draws into `root` and may return a cleanup function; it imports only its own files, by relative paths.

id.description: Language id, unique among this extension’s syntaxes. A chat code block whose fence names it (```gleam), or one of its extensions without the dot, is highlighted with it.

scopeName.description: The grammar’s root scope, unique among this extension’s syntaxes; the grammar file’s own `scopeName` must match.

path.description: A TextMate grammar in JSON, at most 1 MiB. Keys a TextMate engine does not read are dropped; every `#name` it includes must name a rule in a repository.

configuration.description: A language configuration, at most 64 KiB: `comments`, `brackets`, `autoClosingPairs` and `surroundingPairs`, which the editor reads.

extensions.description: File-name suffixes the editor opens in this language, ignoring case. A longer suffix wins over a shorter one, and one of Studio’s own languages that drives completions (TypeScript, JavaScript, JSON, CSS, SCSS, Less, HTML, Markdown) is never replaced.

filenames.description: Exact file names the editor opens in this language, ignoring case; a name wins over any suffix.

syntaxes.description: Syntax highlighting for a language, in chat code blocks and the editor.

id.description: Id, unique among this extension’s editors.

title.description: Its name, in the editor’s Open with menu.

icon.description: Glyph beside its name. Defaults to `extension`.

entry.description: What the editor draws, in a frame of its own in the file’s tab: a `.js` or `.mjs` module whose `mount(root, studio)` draws into `root`. Its `studio.document` holds the file’s content and takes its edits; Studio keeps the unsaved state, saves and watches the file, and the frame never gets a path.

extensions.description: File-name suffixes it opens, with the dot, ignoring case. A longer suffix (`.todo.json`) wins over a shorter one (`.json`), and a file named only the suffix never matches. Give `extensions`, `filenames` or both.

filenames.description: Exact file names it opens, ignoring case; a name wins over any suffix.

priority.description: `default` (the default) opens matching files in this editor; `option` opens them in Studio’s text editor and offers this one under Open with. A file Studio’s own editor has a language for (`.json`, `.ts`, `.py`, `.md`, `package.json` and the like) or shows as an image is always `option`, whether the editor names it by suffix or by name, so installing an extension never changes how a person’s code opens. Either way the person can reopen the file in the text editor.

contentKind.description: `text` (the default) hands the editor the file as UTF-8 text and takes whole-text edits; `bytes` hands it the raw bytes, for a binary format, and takes whole-byte edits.

customEditors.description: Editors for files of a type, drawn in the file’s tab. Needs the `workspace-files:read` permission, and `workspace-files:write` to save; without it the file opens read only.

command.description: The command the key runs. Either a command this extension contributes in `contributes.commands`, or one of Studio’s own command actions (listed below), which a content extension may bind without any code.

key.description: The key chord: modifiers and one key joined by `+`. `Mod` is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. It can be changed or removed in Settings ▸ Shortcuts like any of Studio’s.

when.description: Where the key works. `workspace` only while a workspace is open. Defaults to `global`.

id.description: Id, unique among this extension’s status bar items.

text.description: A short label. Give `text`, `icon` or both.

tooltip.description: Shown on hover. Defaults to the extension’s name.

command.description: The command pressing the item runs. Without one, the item only shows. Either a command this extension contributes in `contributes.commands`, or one of Studio’s own command actions (listed below), which a content extension may bind without any code.

statusBarItems.description: Short status items, shown in the window’s band beside the top bar.

key.description: The key its value is read under (`settings.get` in a frame, `getModuleAppState` in a worker, both with `settings:own`).

default.description: The value read while the person has set none; of `type`.

enum.description: The values allowed, of `type`; Settings shows a picker.

enumLabels.description: The picker’s labels, one per `enum` value.

maxLength.description: Strings: the most characters. Defaults to 4096.

multiline.description: Strings: a box of several lines.

placeholder.description: Strings and numbers: a hint shown while empty.

settings.description: Settings Studio shows under the extension in Settings, with no code of its own; the extension’s code reads their values with `settings:own`.

name.description: The tool’s name on Studio’s MCP server. The worker serves it with `registerMcpTools`; a tool it registers that is not declared here is refused.

description.description: What agents are told the tool does.

access.description: `read` changes nothing; `operate` may, and agents are asked before it runs where their settings say so.

inputSchema.description: The tool’s parameters, as a JSON Schema for an object: what agents see, before the worker has ever run. The schema the worker registers must take no more than this one (no parameter it leaves out, none it requires dropped). A tool that takes none says `{ "type": "object", "properties": {} }`.

mcpTools.description: Tools agents reach through Studio’s MCP server. Needs the `tools:contribute` permission.

point.description: Where Studio asks the worker, which serves it with `registerHooks`. A `.before` point may refuse or change what Studio is about to do; an `.after` point only hears what it did. The guide’s hooks topic says what each one carries.

onError.description: What a failed hook does: one that throws, answers after 2 s, answers something else, or whose worker crashed or did not start. `pass` (the default) lets the action go on as if it had passed; `deny` refuses it, naming the extension, so a guard fails closed. Ignored for an `.after` point.

hooks.description: Hooks the worker runs before (or after) Studio acts: Studio calls them in order, the installed extensions by install key and then the development folders in the order they were registered, waiting at most 2 s on each. The approval names each point in plain words, and an update that adds one asks again.

id.description: Id, unique among this extension’s skills. Agents are handed a copy named `x<8 hex of a hash of the install key>-<skill id>`, its frontmatter holding only `name` and `description`.

path.description: A folder holding the skill: its `SKILL.md` (at most 256 KiB) and any files it names, 256 files at most.

skills.description: Skills the person’s agents can use, in every workspace on this machine. Studio copies each into a folder of its own and hands it to agents at launch; it never writes into a project. Listed when the extension is installed; no approval is asked for them.

id.description: Id, unique among this extension’s servers. Agents see the server as `<publisher>_<id>_<server id>`.

description.description: What it gives agents, in a sentence.

transport.description: `stdio`: a local command each agent starts, with `command`. `http`: a hosted server agents reach at `url`.

command.description: What a `stdio` server runs: a program on the PATH, such as `node` or `npx`, or a file the extension ships, as `${extensionPath}/bin/server`.

args.description: Its arguments. `${extensionPath}` stands for the extension’s installed folder.

value.description: Its value, as written: Studio reads none from its own environment, and a value naming a variable (`${…}`, `{env:…}`) is refused, since an agent would fill it in from the person’s machine. `${extensionPath}` stands for the installed folder.

env.description: Environment variables the command runs with, shown on the install review.

url.description: Where an `http` server is: `https`, or plain `http` to localhost. It names no variable (`${…}`, `{env:…}`): an agent would fill one in from the person’s machine.

mcpServers.description: MCP servers the person’s agents get, in every workspace on this machine. A `stdio` server’s command, arguments, environment and the extension’s files are part of what the person approves at install, so an update that changes any of them asks again; an `http` server is listed when the extension is installed and asks nothing.

id.description: Id, unique among this extension’s providers. Studio knows it, and keeps its key, as `<publisher>.<id>/<provider id>`.

name.description: Its name in the model picker.

baseUrl.description: The OpenAI-compatible API’s base: `https`, or plain `http` to localhost. Its key is sent to this origin and no other, and the install review names it. A path on it is kept: the request paths are joined after it, so `https://api.example.com/openai` and `/v1/chat/completions` make `https://api.example.com/openai/v1/chat/completions`.

chatCompletionsPath.description: The chat completions path, joined after `baseUrl`’s own path. Defaults to `/v1/chat/completions`.

modelsPath.description: A models path, joined after `baseUrl`’s own path, answering `{ data: [{ id }] }`, for the picker to list what the endpoint offers now.

id.description: The model id the endpoint takes.

models.description: Models to offer, the first being the default. At least one.

apiKey.title: ProviderApiKey

label.description: What the key is called where the person enters it, in Settings.

apiKey.description: The provider takes an API key, entered in Settings and sent as a bearer token. Never read from an environment variable.

providers.description: Model providers for chats: OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The person approves each at install, seeing the origin its key goes to; an update that adds one or moves it to another origin asks again.

themes.description: Reserved for app color themes; must be empty.

terminalThemes.description: Reserved for terminal color themes; must be empty.

iconThemes.description: Reserved for file icon themes; must be empty.

fonts.description: Reserved for font families; must be empty.

snippets.description: Reserved for editor snippets; must be empty.

newFiles.description: Reserved for new file templates; must be empty.

events.description: Reserved for events delivered to the worker; must be empty.

sidecars.description: Reserved for background processes; must be empty.

agentProviders.description: Reserved for agent providers run by an extension’s own code; must be empty.

contributes.description: What it adds to Studio. Every point defaults to empty.
